summary: Markus Gabriel is a philosopher who studied at the University of Bonn (~1998–2002). He held posts at the University of Bonn (~2009), UC Berkeley, The New School, and the Kyoto Institute of Philosophy (Global Senior Advisor, 2024).

Markus Viehbeck specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He completed his PhD at the University of Vienna (-2012) under Helmut Tauscher and Franz-Karl Ehrhard, and held posts at Vienna (attested 2011) and Heidelberg University as a project researcher.

Marsha Weidner works in art history, archaeology, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD from the University of California, Berkeley, and held posts at the University of Virginia (attested 1990) and the University of Kansas (attested 2001).

Marshall Sahlins was a scholar in history and archaeology. He studied at the University of Michigan (~1948–1952) and Columbia University (~1952–1954), holding academic posts at the University of Michigan (~1957–1973) and the University of Chicago (from 1973).

Martha Nussbaum is a philosopher who studied at Wellesley, NYU, and Harvard, also studying under Bernard Williams. Her major posts include Harvard (~1975–1982), Brown University (1984–1995), and the University of Chicago and its Law School (from 1995).

Martin Baumann works in religious studies and Buddhist studies. He completed a PhD at Leibniz University Hannover (~1990–1993) and a habilitation at Leipzig University (~1994–1999), becoming a professor of religious studies at the University of Lucerne in 2001.

Martin Brauen is a scholar in Tibetology and history/archaeology. He studied at the University of Delhi, earned a doctorate from the University of Zurich, and served at the Ethnographic Museum at Zurich (from 1975) and Rubin Museum of Art (2008–2012).

Martin Collcutt specializes in Japanology, history, and Buddhist studies. Educated at Cambridge, Fitzwilliam College, and Harvard (PhD 1975), he taught at Yokohama National University, the University of Tokyo, and served at Princeton University (1975–2015).

Martin Delhey works in Indology and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Hamburg under Lambert Schmithausen, holding research posts at Hamburg, Ryukoku University, the International Institute for Buddhist Studies, Göttingen, and Shandong University (2019).

Martin Haug was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Rudolf von Roth and Theodor Benfey at Tübingen, Göttingen, and Bonn. He held posts at Bonn (1854), Deccan College (1859–1866), and the University of Munich (from 1868).

Martin Heidegger was a philosopher who studied at the University of Freiburg under Heinrich Rickert (~1909–1916). He held academic posts at the University of Freiburg (1915–1923, 1928–1958) and the University of Marburg (1923–1928).

Martin Joachim Kümmel is a linguist and Indologist who earned his degrees and habilitation at the University of Freiburg (~1990–2005). He held posts at the University of Freiburg (~1999–2011) and the University of Jena (chair from 2013).

Martin King Whyte is a Sinologist and sociologist. He studied at Cornell and Harvard (PhD 1971), then held faculty positions at Boston University, the University of Michigan (1970–1994), George Washington University (1994–2000), and Harvard University (from 2000).

Martin Lehnert works in Sinology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He completed his PhD at the University of Freiburg and served as Professor of East Asian Religion and Philosophy at the University of Munich (attested 2016).
Martin Lowenthal is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under traditional teachers Tenzin Wangyal Rinpoche and Namkhai Norbu. He has held academic posts at Boston College and Harvard University.

Martin Riesebrodt was a religious studies scholar. He completed his doctorate at Heidelberg (~1970–1973) and habilitation at Munich (~1986–1990), later serving as professor at the University of Chicago (1990–2011) and the Graduate Institute of International and Development Studies (2013).

Martin Seeger is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Hamburg by 2004 under doctoral supervisor Barend Jan Terwiel and held a post at Hamburg (attested 2004).

Martin T. Adam works in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and philosophy. He completed his PhD at McGill University under Richard P. Hayes (attested 2002) and also studied at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies.

Martin Willson was a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied under traditional teachers including Lama Thubten Yeshe, Thubten Zopa Rinpoche, Geshe Thubten Loden, Zasep Tulku Rinpoche, Geshe Rabten, Geshe Jampa Tegchok, and Geshe Lhundub Sopa.

Martina Draszczyk specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied under Lambert Schmithausen for her MA, earned her doctoral degree at the University of Vienna (attested 2012), and held a post at the University of Vienna.
